A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 4RC work. Their complete 15-page contents, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, tracking, depth, and ablation results in Tables 1–4, with streaming and additional benchmark results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the S-4RC streaming evaluation and supplementary tracking and depth comparisons.

M1.justification: The encoder, conditional decoder, geometry/displacement factorization, training objectives, and S-4RC streaming variant are unchanged. The revised architectural description concerns D4RT, a related method.

E1.justification: Training datasets and all evaluated tasks, datasets, and scenarios remain unchanged, including appendix evaluations. Changing Panoptic Studio's abbreviation from PS to PStudio and correcting the TAPVid-3D citation do not change coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding experiment, including Tables 7–8. D4RT remains discussed without being added to the evaluated comparisons; Table 8 only corrects Pi3's citation.

E3.justification: Sampling, training settings, metrics, and alignment procedures are retained. Section 4.3 changes the expansion of ATE from Absolute Trajectory Error to Absolute Translation Error, but reports no changed metric definition or procedure.

E4.justification: The motion-head and output-representation ablations in Table 4 and Figure 5 are unchanged. The streaming evaluation, alternative-alignment comparisons, and qualitative examples were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Both versions report point estimates without adding or removing repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative findings are retained, including appendix Tables 6–8. For example, Table 1 retains 4RC's Kubric APD of 85.44 and EPE of 1.022. Citation corrections do not alter results.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, factorization, decoder equations, and losses in Equations 1–8 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified feed-forward reconstruction, encode-once querying, factorized representation, and empirical performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the results and design mechanisms are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same limitations concerning difficult geometry and extreme or chaotic motion, together with their proposed explanations.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the same architecture, dataset sampling, augmentation, supervision, and hardware details. S-4RC training details and the project-page access information also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the Perceiver-like, contrastive description of D4RT with an explicit account of its global encoding and query decoding, acknowledging architectural similarity to 4RC. The Perceiver reference is removed, and Koppula et al. (2024) is added as the TAPVid-3D reference.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to the D4RT paragraph, dataset and metric terminology, citations, and version dates. Table 8 corrects Pi3's citation from Wang et al. (2025a), which identifies VGGT, to Wang et al. (2025d). Section organization is unchanged.

P2.justification: Reference-list edits cause limited reflow across pages 9–10, and Appendix B.2 has different line wrapping. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–8 retain their arrangement and visual design; no displays are added, removed, or redrawn.

improvement.justification: v2 improves attribution and clarity by explaining D4RT's shared encoder/query-decoder pattern, citing the named TAPVid-3D benchmark, and correcting Pi3's Table 8 reference. These are useful scholarly corrections, while the method, empirical evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
